findings.description: When `git rebase --abort` fails, the empty catch swallows it, and the gate now goes on to merge and land the branch. Before this change the same path stopped with a fail.
findings.body:
**If `rebase --abort` fails, including when a Ctrl-C kills it, the error is lost and the gate merges and lands anyway.**

While the merge lock is held, node ignores SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP (`stayAlive`, L1242-1243). The only way the gate sees an interrupt is through a child's `error.signal`, which `rethrowIfKilled` checks.

**Trigger.** The rebase hits a real conflict and exits with status 1, so its `error.signal` is unset. The operator then presses Ctrl-C while `git rebase --abort` is running. On a large worktree the abort's `reset --hard` takes a while, so this window is real.
- The bare `catch {}` throws away the killed abort's error.
- `rethrowIfKilled(error)` checks only the rebase's error, which was not killed.
- The code sets `step = 'merge'` and calls `mergeTargetInto`.

**What `mergeTargetInto` does next.** The worktree is still in the stopped rebase, so HEAD is detached.
- `symbolic-ref -q HEAD` exits 1, so `head` is undefined.
- The compare-and-swap moves the branch to the merge commit.
- `if (head !== branchRef) return undefined;` counts as a pass.

The gate then runs the remaining stages and fast-forwards the target. Node already swallowed the signal, so nothing later sees the interrupt. This breaks ADR 0190's guarantee that "no merge follows a Ctrl-C".

The same catch also hides an abort that fails for another reason, such as an `index.lock` held by the session's own git. Before this PR that case ended in a worker-facing fail. Now the gate passes and lands while the session's worktree is left mid-rebase on a detached HEAD.

**Fix.**
- **Interrupt case:** `catch (abortError) { rethrowIfKilled(abortError); }`.
- **Other abort failures:** keep the old fail when the abort fails, or merge only once no rebase is in progress, for example once `rebase-merge` is gone from the worktree's admin dir.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/0bacf07759d594f5cf650ce1625f8fe89d5329c3/src/core/merge-gate.service.ts#L2402-L2413

findings.description: No test covers the new guard that stops an interrupted rebase from turning into a merge. If you delete `rethrowIfKilled(error);` at L2410, the whole suite still passes, but an interrupted rebase then merges and lands.
findings.body:
**No test covers the rule that an interrupted rebase is never treated as a conflict.**

After this change, any rebase failure that is not a kill leads to `mergeTargetInto` and then landing. The only thing that stops an operator's Ctrl-C from turning into a merge is `rethrowIfKilled(error)` at `merge-gate.service.ts` L2410.

That line can be deleted without any test failing. A rebase killed by SIGINT would then set `rebaseConflicted = true`, the clean `merge-tree` would pass, and the gate would land. Nothing in the suite catches this:
- `merge-gate-fresh-base.test.ts` covers only real conflicts, clean merges and ancestry-check counts.
- No existing test throws a signal from the `rebase` call. The only test that hooks it (`merge-gate-open-pr.test.ts:438-445`) never throws.

The project already tests interrupts at other points of the merge path, for example `merge-gate-regate.test.ts` L1417 and L1446. They use `beforeGit` to throw `{ signal: 'SIGINT', status: null }`.

Add a matching case with a matcher like `args.includes('rebase') && !args.includes('--abort')`, and assert that:
- `runMergeGate` rejects with the interrupt;
- `steerPane` is not called;
- the branch and `main` are unchanged.

A second case that throws the signal from the `--abort` call would also cover the abort-swallow finding.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/0bacf07759d594f5cf650ce1625f8fe89d5329c3/src/core/merge-gate.service.ts#L2402-L2413

findings.description: `holdsMergeOfTarget` counts any merge commit with a parent in the target's history, not only a merge of the target. A branch whose first commit merges a side branch, or that merged a sibling branch which has since landed, skips a clean rebase and lands an extra merge commit.
"A fresh-base failure the session did not cause no longer happens" claims too much: the fallback merge can still conflict. Say instead that a rebase conflict whose merge is clean no longer fails.

In the `mergeTargetInto` JSDoc, "or one no rebase should rewrite" is vague, and the inserted text runs well past the paragraph's wrap width. Name the case instead: a no-PR branch that holds a merge of the target or whose rebase conflicted (decision 190).

process_issues.description: A `git diff` naming merge-gate.service.ts and merge-gate.test.ts together failed with a bwrap error on .git/config.worktree.lock. The retry for the service file alone worked, but the guards reviewer never saw the merge-gate.test.ts diff.

Not spawned: review-context (no spec/protocol/infra surface), review-workflow-safety (no workflow change), review-spec (no closing reference or spec source), review-maintainability (off the default roster).
